about: The next version put together from two candidates that each passed in ab-run #59: the hooks with free damage (eldrazi-incursion-hooksopen.json) and the limit a turn on the Ulalek trigger (eldrazi-incursion-limit.json). DESIGN.md section 38. Only the playbook object is read.

playbook.notes: Version 2 = the shipped version 1 (its trigger rules and its twelve cast rules, unchanged and in their order: now rules 6 to 17; no attack block, as shipped) with five rules in front for the deck's sweepers, which version 1 left to Forge. Written from the 200 games of the league of twelve (league-run #3, seed 20261250), where the seat won 50. Drawn (games), cast, and in hand on the seat's last own turn of a loss: All Is Dust 51, 16, 18; Selective Obliteration 56, 2, 30 (AI:RemoveDeck:All: Forge never casts it from hand); Kozilek's Return 57, 29, 13. Rules 1-2, All Is Dust: each player sacrifices every coloured permanent, and nearly all of this deck is colourless or devoid (Ulalek included; the coloured permanents are Garruk's Uprising, Awakening Zone and Imprisoned in the Moon), so it is a one-sided wipe. In the league's casts it took 5 to 14 opposing creatures and none to two of ours, and the seat won 13 of the 16 games in which it was cast. Losses with it in hand had 7 to 10 lands beside opposing boards of 8 to 40 creatures (g00253, g00114, g00419, g00464, g00345, g00147). Cast as soon as one opponent has four creatures (the Hail, Caesar threshold for its one-sided Ruinous Ultimatum) or could hit for 12. Rules 3-4, Selective Obliteration: each player keeps only colourless permanents and those of the one colour they choose; multicoloured permanents (commanders such as Caesar or Emmara) go whatever is chosen. Near one-sided for this deck, weaker than All Is Dust against a single-colour opponent (Goblin Storm, Wretched Ranks lose nothing), so it waits for a bigger board: five creatures or a threat of 15. Below All Is Dust so that the full wipe goes first when both can be cast. Rule 5, Kozilek's Return (2 to each creature; it also kills our Scions and Spawn, which are mana, and Glaring Fleshraker): Forge casts it in about half the games it draws it; held at 13 losses, beside opposing token boards of 7 to 50. Cast at sorcery speed once one opponent has five creatures. Not written: Crib Swap, Imprisoned in the Moon, Eldrazi Confluence, Warping Wail, Ugin's -3, Endbringer and Drowner of Hope need targets on the other side; Forge picks them and already casts or uses most (Crib Swap 38 of 50, Warping Wail 51 of 58, Ugin 43 of 62, Imprisoned 24 of 58, Confluence 16 of 53). Ulamog's Nullifier counters at instant speed, outside the rules' reach. Local check, 16 tables of bots (seeds 20263070-20263072, rules firing, not a win rate): All Is Dust cast in both games where 7 mana came while it was in hand (Limit Break, Wretched Ranks and Enduring boards gone at t42; 20 Token Triumph permanents against 2 of ours at t32), won both; Selective Obliteration cast in 4 of the 5 games it was drawn (9 Wretched Ranks and 3 Enduring creatures at t32; 8 Goblin Storm creatures at t34; the fifth game was won without it), Kozilek's Return 2 of 2. None of the three in hand at any of the 6 losses. One table ran into the clock on a Skittering Invasion chain of 127 copies (the version-1 defect, not these rules). Previous notes (version 1): Eldrazi Incursion (Ulalek, Fused Atrocity: whenever you cast an Eldrazi spell, you may pay {C}{C} to copy every spell and every other ability you control). Stock Forge never pays Ulalek's trigger (0 copies in 12 audit games, 63 triggers put on the stack) and casts Ulalek on its own turn 6.5 on average. Rules: Sol Ring, then Ulalek at once, then the other rocks (a rock cast first had cost Ulalek a turn); Sire of Stagnation only while Ulalek is not on the battlefield (held otherwise), because copies of Sire draw two per Sire per opponent land and milled the seat in a tuning game (seven copies); the cost reducers and engines (Herald's Horn, Forsaken Monument, Ugin, Awakening Zone, Garruk's Uprising, Mystic Forge, Dreamstone Hedron), then the creatures dearest first; Ulamog's Dreadsire's 10/10 after combat (vigilance); the draw spells while 30 cards remain; Idol of Oblivion's 10/10 and its draw. Eldrazi Monument is held until five creatures, two of them tokens: its upkeep sacrifice ate Ulalek and the board in a tuning game. Trigger: Ulalek's copy paid while Forge estimates 10 mana or less left, declined above. Each copy of the trigger copies every spell on the stack again, so accepting without the cap doubled one creature spell into a thousand copies and two of twelve games ran into the clock as draws and one into the turn cap; the mana bound caps a chain at about five payments. Go-wide attack from two attackers up. Goldfish: audit seeds 15002-15013 stock 11.33, this file 10.25; tuning seeds 15022-15041 stock 11.65, this file 10.45 (+1.20, 95% +0.76 to +1.64). Validation, seeds 15101-15140, not looked at before the rules were final: stock 11.85 (40 of 40 finished), this file 10.42 (38 of 40), +1.21 turns on the 38 paired seeds (95% +0.74 to +1.68), faster in 24, same in 12, slower in 2. The two unfinished games hit the turn cap: on seed 15132 the mana cap did not stop a chain (Elder Deep-Fiend copied 255 times), and Garruk's Uprising drew a card for each copy until the seat was milled at 126 life. Forge's mana estimate seems to leave out Spawn and Scion sacrifices doubled by Forsaken Monument. Seed 15104 stayed on one land all game. Shipped on 2026-11-12 as version 1 with the attack left to Forge: at 200 tables of bots (ab-run #24, seed 20261230) 64 wins against the stock pilot's 62 (+1.0 points, 95% -7 to +9: level); 52 with the go-wide attack. Open defect: a chain of copies can deck the seat. Shipped as version 2 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #31: on the same 200 tables of bots (seed 20261300, opponents drawn from the other eleven bots under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) it won 63 against version 1's 64 (-0.5 points, 95% -6 to +5, exact test 1.0); the cards the new rules name were cast in 116 of the 138 games they were drawn, under version 1 in 43 of 133. It has not been set against its stock pilot. What it still casts in a share of games 15 points or more below stock AI's (the stock arm of ab-run #26, other tables of the same pool), 15 cards: Eldrazi Conscription, Sire of Stagnation, Everflowing Chalice, Imprisoned in the Moon, Eldrazi Monument, Eldritch Immunity and 9 more (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/pool-answers/eldrazi-incursion-check.txt). VERSION 3 CANDIDATE `hooksopen` (2026-11-21). Version 2 with five changes: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then the creatures that stayed home attack an opponent that has no creature that can block, the most dangerous such opponent first: those that deal damage, have no ability that taps them (or have vigilance) and are not wanted home by Forge's own judgement of the seat's defence (`"open": true`; a weaker opponent is not killed this way while a more dangerous one lives); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); and then a triggered ability of the seat that removes one permanent of an opponent (destroys it, exiles it, returns it to hand or library) is aimed at the opponent that looks most dangerous, when that opponent looks more dangerous than the one Forge aimed at by five or more and has a permanent of the same kind worth at least as much as Forge's choice or at least 4 (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`); and then when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). No cast or trigger rule is changed. WITH THE LIMIT (2026-11-22): VERSION 3 CANDIDATE `limit` (2026-11-22). Version 2 with a limit a turn on its Ulalek trigger rule; no cast rule is changed. WHY: Ulalek, Fused Atrocity's trigger (whenever you cast an Eldrazi spell, you may pay two colourless: copy all spells you control, then all your other activated and triggered abilities) doubles what is on the stack each time it is paid for, its own waiting triggers included. Version 2 pays whenever ten mana or fewer are at hand, as often as the trigger comes: in the 2,400 games of ab-run #58 (the pool's twelve under their shipped playbooks) fourteen ended without a winner in such a chain, with 64 to 512 copies of one spell or a thousand of one trigger in the last turn, on the clock, in a draw or in a Forge exception, wherever the deck sat. A person pays for it once or twice a turn. THE RULE (harness 0.4.11, `per_turn`): yes at most three times in one turn, then no until the next turn, so one spell becomes eight at most. BEFORE ITS EXAM (2026-11-21): the four tables of the deck's own arm of ab-run #58 that ended without a winner were replayed under this file (tables 53, 101, 110 and 133 of seed 20261400): all four games finished, the first event at which each differs from the original is where the limit first said no, the limit was reached 3 to 9 times a game, and the seat won three. At the tables beside the shipped arm in ab-run #59 (the rule is in CLAUDE.md, In flight). In ab-run #59 the limit by itself (version 2 with it) won 76 tables of 200 where version 2 won 77 (9 tables against 10), left one game without a winner where version 2 left four, and all four tables the chain had broken finished (three won); the limit was reached on 94 of the 200 tables, 241 times. This file is the `hooksopen` arm of that run with the same trigger rules: two parts that each passed by itself and were not played together; the next run at the pool's tables (ab-run #62, where this deck sits among the opponents) is the first to play them together, and the league of twelve after it is their confirming run.
